ActorType.description:
Who performed the action. `User` is a tenant user; `PlatformAdmin` is an
operator on the platform host; `System` is an automated process (jobs,
lifecycle sweeps).

external_id.description:
The platform's own id for this ad, once one has been recorded — the
only key that correlates a review observation (which arrives keyed by
platform id) back onto this ad. `None` for ads the platform has never
echoed an id for; a platform that assigns ids at creation must persist
them here, or its verdicts can never be matched.

review.description:
Last review observation pulled from the platform. Absent (pending,
never checked) until a poll happens — ads only get reviewed once they
are published.

AdReview.description:
The platform's review verdict for one ad. `reasons` preserves the
platform's own policy wording verbatim — a paraphrased rejection is worse
than useless when the tenant has to fix the ad in the native tool.

AdReviewStatusView.description:
One ad's refreshed review state, addressed by its platform-facing id so a
client can correlate against the campaign tree it already has.

AdvertisingProblemType.description: Stable RFC-7807 suffixes emitted by future advertising endpoints.

birth_year.description: Declared birth year; `is_minor` wins when present.

authorization_evidence.description: Signed permission artifact: an opaque reference plus checksum.

ApiError.description:
Application-level API error.

Contexts map their domain errors into these at the adapter boundary; the
HTTP status lives in exactly one place (here), never scattered across
handlers.

oneOf.description:
A conflict carrying a machine-readable `reason`, surfaced as
`ProblemDetail.reason`, so a client can distinguish conflicts of the
same status without parsing `detail` — cap version races, for
example, where missing-precondition and lost-race need different
recovery. The status and `type` stay the plain conflict class.

ConflictReasoned.description:
A conflict carrying a machine-readable `reason`, surfaced as
`ProblemDetail.reason`, so a client can distinguish conflicts of the
same status without parsing `detail` — cap version races, for
example, where missing-precondition and lost-race need different
recovery. The status and `type` stay the plain conflict class.

Appeal.description: The appeal aggregate (US states with an appeal right).

authority.description: The state authority's complaint route, included up front.

ApprovalView.description: One approval request as exposed by the API.

AuditEntry.description:
A chained audit entry.

`seq` is the chain's ordering authority (assigned by the database on
INSERT); it is deliberately *not* covered by the hash because the
database assigns it after the hash is computed. Ordering integrity comes
from the append-only grants + trigger; content and link integrity from
the hash chain.

AvailableThemeView.description: A theme in the tenant-facing catalog (entitlement-filtered).

BlockerView.description: One reason the connection cannot take payments yet, keyed for i18n.

digest.description: The sha256 digest of the stored bytes (content-addressed file name).

BrandAssetKind.description: The brand asset kinds a tenant can upload.

BrandAssetUrls.description: Absolute URLs for a tenant's brand assets.

BreachIncident.description: A breach incident aggregate; obligations are computed per jurisdiction.

BreachRuleSet.description:
Breach-notification rules per jurisdiction. jsonb in the database so a
new law is a data change; typed here so the calculator cannot misparse.

authority_due_days.description:
Deadline to notify the authority, in days (states without an
hour-level rule).

authority_due_hours.description: Deadline to notify the supervisory authority, in hours.

authority_threshold.description:
Minimum number of affected subjects before the authority must be
notified at all (several US states).

consumer_due_days.description: Deadline to notify consumers, in days.

consumer_threshold.description: Minimum affected count before consumers must be notified.

encryption_safe_harbour.description:
Whether encryption-at-rest of the compromised data suppresses the
obligations this rule set marks as encryption-exempt (safe harbour).

BuildDetails.description:
Release stamp for field measurements (`GET /api/v1/system/build`,
FR-1102): the exact build that served a response, so a latency sample
from RUM, the error tracker, or a status page can always be attributed.
Carries no tenant data and nothing but the four stamp fields.

commit.description: Git commit the binary was built from.

environment.description:
Deployment environment the process was configured for
(`local`, `staging`, `production`).

version.description: Semantic version of the running binary.

BuildInfo.description: Immutable build/version information, captured at compile time.

commit.description: Git commit the binary was built from (set by the build pipeline).

rust_version.description: Rust toolchain the binary was compiled with.

service_name.description: OTel service name of this deployment unit.

version.description: Semantic version of the running binary.

unmatched_platform_ads.description:
What the platform listed that this campaign's tree cannot account
for. Non-empty means the poll could not fully correlate — an
all-pending `ads` list alongside platform-listed ids here is a
correlation gap, not a clean "everything still in review".

CampaignView.description:
One campaign plus the envelope fields the domain model does not carry:
which connection it belongs to and the platform-assigned id once
published.

CapabilityMatrix.description: Data consumed by both the validator and the frontend form engine.

text_limits.description: Locale -> field name -> inclusive character limit.

CatalogView.description:
The catalog the frontend consumes: every message for one domain in one
locale, plus a revision (ETag) that changes whenever content does.

ChallengeView.description:
The challenge as shown to the tenant (the token itself is the secret
they must publish; the value is pre-rendered for copy-paste).

CheckoutConfigView.description:
What the storefront needs before it can render a Pay button:
readiness and the settlement currency. Derived from the tenant's live
connection by the same gate the checkout itself applies.

cannot_accept_reason.description:
The i18n key for *why* not (`payments.blocker.*`), so the
storefront can show a reason next to a disabled button instead of
waiting for a 409. `null` when payments are accepted.

currency.description:
The connected account's settlement currency. The storefront must
price in this currency; anything else is refused at creation.

tax_enabled.description:
Whether a checkout started now would have automatic tax applied,
read from the tenant's stored tax settings by the same rule the
session creation applies. The storefront renders its tax note from
this; it never assumes tax is on.

CheckoutView.description:
The checkout as the storefront sees it. `status` is the only source
the confirmation page trusts: derived from webhook-recorded truth,
never from the redirect.

failure_code.description:
Server-issued exactly once per order when paid; identical on every
refresh of the confirmation page, so phase 10's conversion
pipeline cannot double-count.
The provider's decline/failure code for the newest failed attempt
(`card_declined`, `insufficient_funds`, …), so the storefront can
tell a buyer *why*. The provider's own message is deliberately not
exposed: the storefront renders its own localized copy.

url.description:
The provider-hosted payment URL, while the checkout can still be
paid. Absent once terminal.

role.description: `primary` (default when the tenant has none), `alias` or `redirect`.

CollectionState.description: Our dunning machine, orthogonal to Stripe's status.

CompleteUploadRequest.description:
Wire-only shape for completing a multipart upload. Same treatment as
[`PresignPartsRequest`]: the use case takes the bare parts vec.

stalled.description:
Ingestion is older than the configured freshness threshold — the
dashboard's "sync failed" / "still updating" state, never presented
as current.

ConnectionSessionView.description:
A short-lived Account Session for the embedded onboarding component.
Fetched per render; never persisted, never logged, single-render.

client_secret.description:
The provider's embedded-components client secret. Handle like a
credential: no caching, no logging, one render.

components.description:
The embedded components enabled on this session:
`account_onboarding`, `notification_banner`, and `account_management`.

ConsentMethod.description: How consent was recorded (drives proof requirements).

ConsentModel.description:
How non-essential processing may start: permission first (EU/UK/JP) or
notice with an honoured refusal (US states).

ConsentSnapshot.description: Capture-time directive proof required by every outbound upload.

propertyNames.description: Adapter-owned identifier. Domain code never switches on a platform name.

CreateCheckoutRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/tenant/checkout` — create a checkout session on the
tenant's connected account (09.4, direct charges). Idempotency-Key is
required: a double-clicked buy button must not create two sessions.

currency.description:
ISO-4217 code; must match the connected account's settlement
currency.

customer_ref.description:
Free-form customer/order context (provider-passthrough; no card
data ever). Rate limiting buckets one key per distinct value.

locale.description: Presentation locale for the hosted page (`ja`, `en-US`, …).

reference.description: The merchant's order reference, echoed on every read model.

success_url.description:
Redirect target on a **verified** tenant domain (phase 08). A
success URL on any other host is rejected outright.

image_required.description:
Placement-set-level requirement (whether at least one image asset is required for the placement set).
Not enforced per asset.

cert_expires_at.description:
The active certificate's expiry, when one has been issued. `None`
while the domain has no active cert (not yet issued, or removed).

DataClass.description:
A data class: the granularity at which the data map, retention rules and
breach classification operate. The registry below is the compile-time
data map; every provider names its classes from it.

DependencyStatus.description: Result of probing one dependency for readiness.

DirectiveSnapshot.description: The full resolved state for one subject.

DirectiveSource.description:
Where a directive's state came from. The jurisdiction profile supplies
the default; everything else is an explicit subject action or signal.

DirectiveState.description: The resolved answer for one purpose.

DisputeView.description: One dispute plus its dashboard deep link (read-only).

DomainFailure.description: Why a domain failed or degraded, as a stable code plus free detail.

routing_ok.description: Same as `txt_ok`, for the routing (CNAME/A) check.

txt_ok.description:
The last verification attempt's independent TXT-ownership result.
`None` when this failure isn't a verification failure, or the check
didn't run that attempt (not "passed").

DomainQuote.description: One search hit: a hostname candidate with normalized pricing.

DsrKind.description:
A DSR kind. `KnowCategories` is the CCPA "right to know" (categories
only, no contents).

EntitlementGrant.description:
One plan → feature grant. Feature keys reference the access context's
catalog (validated at write time; no FK because the catalog is runtime
data).

FeatureView.description: One catalog feature as exposed by the API.

FontSpec.description:
A font the theme uses. Self-hosted only — no remote `@import` is ever
possible through this schema.

ImpersonationGrantView.description: One grant as exposed by the API.

ImpersonationMode.description:
How much the impersonated session may do (mirrors the HTTP layer's
mode; the adapter converts).

InstallThemeVersionCommand.description:
The command a theme artifact resolves to after the publish pipeline
validated it (manifest schema, token schema, contrast gate).

allow_contrast_warnings.description: Explicit override for the contrast gate (recorded, never silent).

artifact_digest.description: sha256 digest the artifact must match.

publisher.description: Who published (first-party "sanvi" or a future third party).

required_feature.description: For premium themes: the entitlement key.

InstructionRecord.description: One instruction record with a localized explanation line.

InvoiceView.description: An invoice row as served to the billing UI.

JurisdictionRef.description:
A jurisdiction code (`eu`, `uk`, `jp`, `us-ca`, …). Parsed, never
free-form, so a typo fails at the boundary rather than silently falling
back to the most protective profile.

LayoutOverride.description: A tenant's layout adjustment: which slots to hide on an unlocked layout.

LayoutSpec.description: A layout definition: named slots and whether tenants may restructure it.

LegalBasis.description: A legal basis for processing a data class.

LegalHold.description: A legal hold: blocks erasure for the named scope until released.

Locale.description:
A validated, canonicalised BCP-47 language tag.

Canonicalisation: language lowercase, script title-case, region
uppercase (`ja-jp` → `ja-JP`, `EN` → `en`). Only well-formed tags
accepted: 2–3 letter language, optional 4-letter script, optional 2-letter
or 3-digit region. This is deliberately *not* full BCP-47 (no variants,
no extensions): the backend only needs the granularity it can translate
and format with.

LocalizedName.description: Localised display names in a manifest.

MembershipSummary.description:
One tenant `GET /api/v1/me` reports the caller as a member of, with the
roles/permissions they hold there — the single hydration call the
frontend's session store and `can()`/`<Can>` are built on (see
`sanvi-frontend/docs/phase-02-auth-ux`), so it carries everything a tenant
switcher and permission-aware render need without a per-tenant follow-up
request.

permissions.description:
The union of every permission `role_ids` grants — a UX hint only; the
backend enforces every mutation independently of what this list says.

MetricPoint.description:
One rollup row (TASK-016, slice 10.7). The grain depends on the
request's `group_by`: `campaign` populates both `platform` and
`campaign_id`; `platform` populates only `platform`; `tenant` leaves
both `None`. Tenant is supplied by the authenticated route scope.

`conversion_value` (the platform's own attribution) and `sanvi_revenue`
(Sanvi's order-based view) are always both present, always labelled
separately — never blended into one number (NFR-1006). Same for
`roas_platform`/`roas_sanvi`: each is `null` on zero spend, never `∞`.

conversion_value.description:
Platform-reported conversion value — attribution the ad platform's
own model made.

restating.description:
Still inside the platform's restatement window — this day's numbers
may still change on a later ingest.

sanvi_revenue.description:
Sanvi's own order-based revenue view. Never summed with
`conversion_value` — see the type's doc comment.

MetricsSummaryRow.description:
One currency's totals across the whole requested range — the range
itself collapsed, so unlike [`MetricPoint`] there is one row per
currency, not per day.

restating.description:
`true` if any day in the range is still inside its platform's
restatement window.

MoneyView.description:
A stored amount is always integer minor units plus the originating ad
account's ISO-4217 currency. JPY ¥2,000 is represented as `2000` / `JPY`.

NoticeAtCollectionView.description:
The notice at collection (served before any collection happens): the
categories collected, the purposes, sale/share status and retention
summary.

redirect_uri.description:
Must match the `redirect_uri` sent to `start` — the platform rejects
a mismatch at exchange time.

tracking_template.description:
`None` leaves the stored value unchanged; there is no way to clear it
back to unset in this slice (same limitation `PATCH /campaigns/{id}`
has for `schedule`).

PatchCampaignRequest.description:
A merge patch: every field is optional and `None` leaves the stored
value unchanged. Used both by `PATCH` and by `validate`'s dry run.

PaymentDetailView.description:
The payment detail the support UI renders: payment + its refunds +
disputes + timeline.

The timeline is a first-class projection derived from stored events
(created, succeeded/failed, refunded, disputed, paid out), each with
a timestamp and an actor where one exists.

PaymentView.description: One payment as the tenant sees it in the list.

fee_minor.description:
The provider-reported fee on this payment. When the platform's
application fee is enabled for the tenant, this is where it is
disclosed — a platform fee the merchant cannot see is not
acceptable, whatever the contract says.

payout_status.description:
Payout status once payout reconciliation includes this payment
(`pending` | `paid` | `failed`; null until then).

PayoutView.description:
One payout as the tenant's list renders it. Read-only: payout
management lives in the provider's own dashboard / embedded component.

status.description:
`pending` | `paid` | `failed`. A failed payout is alerted, not
just listed — the tenant's money is stuck at the provider.

payouts.description: Newest first; empty before a connection exists.

Period.description: A billing period (current or invoice period).

PermissionScope.description: Who a permission applies to, which decides how the check resolves.

hostname.description: The hostname to purchase (must be an apex: `acme.com`).

idempotency_key.description:
Client-supplied idempotency key: retrying a purchase returns the
original order instead of charging twice.

PlanAdminView.description: The operator view adds the Stripe ids and visibility.

PlanPriceView.description: One price on the public pricing page.

PlanTier.description:
One sellable tier. Each tier maps to exactly one Stripe Product so
Checkout line items show a distinguishable name.

PlanVisibility.description: Whether a plan appears on the public pricing page.

PlatformFeeDisclosure.description:
The platform's fee disclosure for this tenant (their payment settings).
A platform fee the merchant cannot see is not acceptable, whatever the
contract says.

enabled.description: Fees are off for this tenant unless stated here.

PlatformKey.description: Adapter-owned identifier. Domain code never switches on a platform name.

PlatformView.description:
Registry-derived catalog item. A platform without entitlement remains in
the list so clients can render its upgrade state rather than a dead end.

PlatformsView.description:
Stable envelope for the platform catalog. TASK-010 fills this only from
registered capability matrices; no platform name is hard-coded here.

PresignPartsRequest.description:
Wire-only shape for presigning multipart upload parts. This has no
counterpart in `domain::dto` because it is not a value the domain layer
needs to model — the use case takes the bare `Vec<i64>`.

PriceInterval.description: Billing variant of a plan: monthly vs annual, currency, amount.

allOf.description:
RFC 9457 extension members for problem classes that carry
structured extras (the disconnect conflict names its blockers,
for example). Flattened onto the JSON object exactly as the RFC
prescribes; carrying them here keeps the error-enrichment layer
from stripping them. Absent otherwise.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation of this specific occurrence.

instance.description: URI of the offending resource, if any.

reason.description:
Machine-readable reason for statuses that carry one (e.g. tenant
suspension); absent otherwise.

status.description: HTTP status code (mirrors the response code).

trace_id.description: Correlates with the request id and the trace in OpenObserve.

type.description: Stable URI identifying the error class.

ProblemDetail.description: RFC 9457 problem detail. This is the only error body the API produces.

ProcessingActivity.description:
An Art. 30 processing record (versioned; the active row describes the
current processing).

ProcessingPurpose.description:
A processing purpose. `Essential` can never be denied and is never
consentable; everything else resolves through the directive engine.

ProviderView.description:
One connectable provider as the settings page renders it. Derived
from the adapter's [`crate::domain::ports::ProviderDescriptor`] —
never hardcoded per provider anywhere in this layer or the handlers.

display_name.description: Human-readable name for cards and menus.

requires_onboarding.description: Whether connecting requires an onboarding flow.

supported_countries.description: ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 countries whose tenants may connect.

ProvidersView.description:
`GET /api/v1/tenant/payments/providers` — the catalog envelope,
derived from the provider registry.

providers.description: Connectable providers, in stable kind order.

PublicPlanView.description:
A plan with its prices and entitlement grants (public pricing page; the
Stripe price ids are omitted — they are integration details).

PurposeDirective.description:
One resolved answer per purpose, with the provenance the privacy centre
renders.

Readiness.description: Aggregate readiness answer: every dependency's status plus the verdict.

oneOf.description: Minor-unit amount or `null` for a full refund (remaining amount).

note.description: Optional free-form note (support context, not the audit reason).

reason.description:
Why the refund is being issued — required, audited and shown in
the timeline. Empty is rejected.

Regime.description:
The legal regime a jurisdiction belongs to; drives nothing by itself —
every decision reads the profile's model fields instead.

RegistrantContact.description:
The registrant contact data (purchase journey). Personal data: minimized,
registered in the phase-05 data map with the registrar as sub-processor,
and erasable subject to ICANN retention rules.

reason.description: The audited reason for the force-release.

RenderedMoneyView.description:
A presentation-only conversion. Converted money is never persisted; its
rate date is required so chart and report values stay explainable.

RequirementEntryView.description:
One outstanding provider requirement, with the i18n message key the
frontend renders it from. The mapping is data
(`payments.requirement_keys`); a code the map has not learned falls
back to `payments.req.unmapped`, whose catalog entry shows the raw code
plus Stripe's requirements help link — new requirements degrade,
never break.

RequirementsView.description:
The connection's outstanding-requirements summary, projected with
render keys.

ResolutionSource.description:
How the tenant was resolved. Most-specific sources win; the source is
recorded on the context for observability and debugging.

ResolvedEntitlementView.description: One resolved entitlement as exposed to a tenant.

ResolvedLayout.description: A layout after tenant adjustments (hidden slots removed).

ResolvedTheme.description: The fully resolved theme document, ready for the frontend.

custom_css.description: Sanitised tenant CSS, scoped under the storefront wrapper class.

dark_tokens.description: The merged dark token tree, when the theme ships dark mode.

etag.description: ETag: hash of (theme, version, revision, locale, api).

revision.description: The live revision this document reflects (draft previews: 0).

tokens.description: The merged nested token tree (light mode).

RetentionAction.description: What the retention sweep does when a class's period expires.

RetentionRule.description: A retention rule (one row of the data map's operational half).

RiskAssessment.description: A DPIA / US state data-protection assessment.

RoleView.description: One role as exposed by the API.

SensitiveModel.description:
How sensitive-personal-information processing starts: permission first,
a "limit my use" directive (CA), or notice only.

SensitivityClass.description:
The sensitivity class of a mapped personal-data field. Drives the CA
"limit use" right, the non-CA opt-in for sensitive data, and the flagged
health-data and minors classes that trigger consent-first handling.

basis_points.description: Basis points of the charge total (1..=10000).

enabled.description: Master switch. Enabling without a component is a validation error.

fixed_amount_minor.description: Flat component in minor units, applied to charges in its currency.

reason.description: Why the change is being made — audited with the actor.

settings.description: Key → value map to upsert. Values are uninterpreted JSON.

SlugAvailability.description: The bare-boolean answer to a slug availability question.

unconvertible_spend_currencies.description:
Currencies for which spend data could not be converted to the cap currency
because an FX rate was unavailable. When non-empty, spend totals are incomplete.

timezone.description:
The tenant calendar timezone the report's period windows were
computed in (resolved from the tenant's locale settings). Surfaced on
the report so clients holding advertising access — but not
locale-settings access — render projections on the same clock
enforcement uses.

kratos_flow_id.description: The Kratos login flow that collided (correlation only).

expires_in_secs.description: How long the challenge stays valid, in seconds.

nonce.description:
The nonce the frontend stores in the `sanvi_link_intent` cookie
(`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, TTL = the intent's).

SubProcessor.description:
A sub-processor registry row. `role` is the field that turns an
ad-platform upload into a "sale"/"share" under US law — it is required
and asserted by phase 10's uploads.

SubjectIdentifier.description:
One identifier by which a subject can be looked up (email, platform user
id, tenant-internal customer id, …).

SubjectInput.description: The subject a request targets, as supplied by the requester.

oneOf.description:
Age signal for the minor rules (e.g. declared age or a guardian
attestation payload).

evidence.description:
Jurisdiction evidence, most trusted first (country codes: `DE`,
`GB`, `US-CA`, …).

SubjectKeyRef.description:
Enough of the capturing subject's identity to rebuild the exact
`SubjectRef` a later withdrawal re-check must query — without ever
persisting the raw email/phone TASK-014 forbids in this context. A
device ref, a tenant's own customer ref, and a platform user id are not
themselves the raw PII that rule targets, so they are stored verbatim;
an email-identified (`Contact`) subject stores nothing reconstructable,
and the retry path refuses rather than re-deriving a directive answer
against the wrong subject.

oneOf.description:
Captured under an email-identified subject. No key material is
stored; a later withdrawal re-check has nothing safe to query and
must refuse rather than guess.

SubjectKind.description: Who the personal data belongs to, relative to the platform.

SubjectRef.description:
The cross-context reference to a data subject. `key` is the canonical,
stable key used for directive materialisation and crypto-shredding:
`user:{snowflake}`, `end_user:{tenant_id}:{external_id}`, `email:{addr}` or
`device:{device_ref}`.

effective_immediately.description:
Opt-out kinds take effect immediately and never require
verification.

verification_required.description: Present when verification is required before disclosure/deletion.

verification_token.description:
Opaque half of the verification credential. The OTP is delivered
out-of-band, so neither response nor notification is sufficient alone.

SubscriptionView.description: The tenant's subscription as served to the billing UI.

SuspendTenantRequest.description: Request body for suspending a tenant.

reason.description: Machine-readable reason: billing | abuse | legal | operational.

Targeting.description: Typed extension data. Arbitrary JSON is deliberately not admitted to the domain.

disclaimer.description: Always present, always the same: we never advise.

liability_account.description:
The liable connected-account id when enabled (`{ type: 'account' }`
routing) — with direct charges the connected account is the
merchant of record.

oneOf.description:
The platform's fee on this tenant's payments, when one is enabled
(off by default in 0.10.0). Disclosed here and on every affected
payment — a platform fee the merchant cannot see is not acceptable,
whatever the contract says.

TenantAdminPageView.description: One page of the operator tenant search.

TenantAdminView.description: One row of the platform admin tenant search.

active_impersonations.description: Active impersonation grants into this tenant.

TenantContext.description:
What a tenant looks like at request time — the shape every context reads
from request extensions.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page (null on the last page).

TenantRuntimeStatus.description:
Tenant lifecycle state as observed at runtime. Only `Active` tenants serve
traffic; `Suspended` returns 423 except on the allow-list.

TenantThemeView.description: The tenant's draft (or live) theme state.

test.description:
Always `true` — a marker so this synthetic call is never mistaken
for a real event by anything reading the response.

ThemeAdminView.description: A registry entry for the platform control plane.

ThemeAssetUrls.description: Theme-provided reference assets (preview/screenshots), resolved to URLs.

ThemeSpecView.description:
Theme reference data surfaced to the tenant UI (fonts/layouts the theme
ships, so the editor knows what is overridable).

ThemeState.description: Draft or live — the two rows a tenant may hold.

ThemeStatus.description: Lifecycle status of a theme in the catalog.

ThemeVersionAdminView.description: A version row for the platform control plane.

ThemeVisibility.description: Who can see a theme in the catalog.

TimelineEntry.description: One entry in the payment's timeline.

actor.description:
Who caused this entry, when a human exists (refunds). Webhook-
derived entries have no actor — the provider did.

oneOf.description:
Money attached to the entry (payment total, refund portion,
dispute amount), when relevant.

detail.description:
Human detail (failure code, refund reason, dispute reason,
status detail), when relevant.

mappings.description: event name -> (platform key -> the platform's conversion action)

TranslationPatch.description: One override in a PUT body.

UnmatchedPlatformAds.description:
What the platform listed that this campaign's tree cannot account for.
A published campaign whose ads were never pushed (or whose platform ids
were never recorded) can never match the platform's listings — surfacing
the gap is what keeps an all-pending response from reading as a clean,
successful poll when it is really "nothing correlated".

ads_without_platform_id.description:
Ads in the campaign tree with no recorded platform id — these can
never match anything until the platform's ids are persisted onto them.

platform_ad_ids.description: Platform-listed ad ids that matched no ad in the campaign tree.

acting_locale.description:
The locale the change was made under (the admin's negotiated
locale), carried on the event so downstream work renders correctly.

enabled.description:
Enable requires the compliance preflight to pass right now; disable
always succeeds (and is a tenant-facing change requiring notice:
mid-period it changes what customers are charged).

UpdateTenantThemeDraftCommand.description:
The edit command. Every field is optional: `None` leaves it unchanged;
`custom_css: Some(None)` removes custom CSS.

layout_overrides.description: Layout adjustments (hidden slots on unlocked layouts).

theme_key.description:
Switch theme. When present with no `version`, pins the theme's
latest published version.

version.description: Explicit version pin (a theme upgrade is never implicit).

UploadBrandAssetCommand.description:
The upload command: base64 payload with a declared media type (the
declared type is advisory — the bytes are sniffed and must match).

get.description:
Gated two ways: the `payments.enabled` phase flag (route absent when off)
and `payments.read` (permission extractor). Deliberately **not** gated on
the `payments.stripe_connect` entitlement, unlike every other payments
route — the catalog is how an un-entitled tenant learns which providers
exist and therefore what upgrading would buy; the admin renders the cards
with the connect CTA replaced by an upgrade prompt. Connecting
(`POST /payments/connections`) keeps the entitlement.

A 403 here therefore means the caller lacks `payments.read` — a
permission problem, not a plan problem. The frontend must not answer it
with an upgrade prompt.

The response is derived from the provider registry — the handler adds
nothing provider-specific. The tenant's country (from the tenant
context's region, when it parses as ISO-3166-1 alpha-2) decides
per-tenant availability; an unparseable region leaves the provider
available rather than locking the tenant out.

tags.description: Tenant payment providers (Stripe Connect, direct charges — Sanvi is never the merchant of record). Money is minor units + ISO-4217 (JPY is zero-decimal). Problem types: payments/provider-unavailable, payments/provider-auth, payments/provider-rate-limited, payments/invalid-country, payments/country-unsupported, payments/connection-exists, payments/connection-not-active, payments/capability-missing, payments/currency-unsupported, payments/idempotency-conflict. Every mutating endpoint requires an Idempotency-Key header; connection creation keys the provider-side idempotency chain, so retries adopt instead of duplicate. Account Session secrets are never persisted or logged.
tags.name: payments

tags.description: Tenant advertising. Money is integer minor units paired with ISO-4217 account currency; rendered FX values carry their rate date. Problem types: advertising/platform-unavailable, advertising/connection-not-active, advertising/capability-unsupported, advertising/token-expired, advertising/directive-suppressed, advertising/budget-cap-reached. Every mutating endpoint requires Idempotency-Key.
tags.name: advertising

tags.description: Tenant media assets: multipart upload (presign/complete), asset reads/deletes and delivery URLs via hitox-media-service. Upstream failures surface as problems carrying a `code` extension member.
